mutants.why: unpackHid extracts the heap-allocation index at (hn_id >> 5); over-shifting by one bit corrupts every legacy-Unicode HID's hid_index so readHeapOnNode resolves the wrong (or zero -> empty) allocation. reusableMessagingFixtureListsMessageViaContentsTable reads the message PC via these heap allocations and asserts prop.display_value == QStringLiteral("FUZZ") (QVERIFY2(found_subject,...)) and items->size()==1; a mis-indexed heap read breaks both.

a valid HID index runs 1..alloc_count; relaxing the guard to >= rejects the highest allocation of every heap (returns empty), which is load-bearing in the contents-table row matrix / message PC. reusableMessagingFixtureListsMessageViaContentsTable asserts items->size()==1 and the Subject reads back as "FUZZ" (QVERIFY2(found_subject,...)); dropping the top allocation fails one of those.

HNPAGEMAP allocation N spans [rgibAlloc[N-1], rgibAlloc[N]); dropping the -1 makes entry_offset == next_offset so every allocation resolves a zero-length span (start==end -> empty mid). reusableMessagingFixtureListsMessageViaContentsTable then reads an empty row matrix and message PC: items->size()==1 and the "FUZZ" Subject assertion (QVERIFY2(found_subject,...)) both fail.

a TCROWID record is dwRowID(key,+0) then dwRowIndex(data,+4); reading +0 returns the row's dwRowID (0x24 in the fixture) instead of logical row 0, so tcRowOffset computes block_u=0x24>=block_count and returns -1, dropping the only live row. rowIndexedTcFixtureListsMessageViaLiveRowBth asserts items->size()==1 and items->first().node_id == kMessageNid.

each TCROWID record is 8 bytes (dwRowID+dwRowIndex); a 4-byte stride makes the single 8-byte leaf parse as two records, appending a bogus second live-row index. rowIndexedTcFixtureListsMessageViaLiveRowBth asserts items->size()==1, which fails once a duplicate/garbage row is materialized.

an HNID-resolvable TC column whose 4-byte cell is an HID must be resolved through the heap (cb_data == 4); inverting the size test skips resolveHnid so the Subject cell surfaces the raw HID bytes instead of the heap string. hnidCellTcFixtureResolvesHeapValue asserts items->first().subject == QStringLiteral("HI").

the Cell Existence Block bit is 1 for a present cell; inverting the test marks the live Subject cell absent so it is never read and prop.display_value stays empty. hnidCellTcFixtureResolvesHeapValue asserts items->first().subject == QStringLiteral("HI"), which then reads empty.

a row's byte offset is block_start + row_in_block*row_size; for the single row (row_in_block==0) the multiply is 0 but the additive mutant yields row_size, pushing the read one row past the matrix so tcRowOffset's own bound (off+row_size>block_end) returns -1 and the row is skipped. reusableMessagingFixtureListsMessageViaContentsTable asserts items->size()==1.

a row occupying exactly [off, off+row_size) is in-bounds when off+row_size == block_end; changing > to >= rejects that legal final row, so the single-row contents matrix (block_end == row_size, off == 0) yields no rows. reusableMessagingFixtureListsMessageViaContentsTable asserts items->size()==1.

an IPM.Note message class must classify as Email; remapping the first prefix entry to Contact changes the enriched summary's item_type. loadFolderItemsEnrichesSenderAndClass asserts captured.first().item_type == sak::EmailItemType::Email for a store whose message class is IPM.Note.

a TCROWID BTH is only walkable when its root HID is nonzero; inverting the zero-guard rejects the valid nonzero root, returns no live rows, and buildTcRows fails a hid_row_index!=0 table closed to zero rows. rowIndexedTcFixtureListsMessageViaLiveRowBth asserts items->size()==1 (and items->first().node_id == kMessageNid).

propertyIdToName stamps MapiProperty::property_name (a human-readable label) on the public parse path (parsePropertyRecords line 2161, surfaced via readItemProperties); blanking every KNOWN-property name makes propertyIdToName return an empty QString for mapped ids. messagePropertyExposesHumanReadableName parses buildMessagingUnicodeStore and asserts the Subject property's property_name == QStringLiteral("PR_SUBJECT") (kPropIdSubject 0x0037 -> PR_SUBJECT in corePropertyNameTable), so the blanked name reads back empty and fails the assert.
